description: The plot illustrates how the number of “Shared Experts for Two Samples” varies with “Sample Token Count” for six labeled series (Intent, Summary, Law, Translation, Code, Math). The x-axis is labeled “Sample Token Count” and uses a logarithmic base-2 scale with tick labels from \(2^9\) through \(2^{20}\) at increments of one exponent. The y-axis is labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” appears linear, and spans roughly from about 2.0 up to about 6.0 with regularly spaced tick marks every 0.5. The Intent series is shown as a solid orange line without markers, rising from about 3.8 at \(2^9\) to about 6.0 by \(2^{19}\)–\(2^{20}\), with a dip near \(2^{11}\) (around 3.9) and then a steady climb toward ~5.6–6.0 from \(2^{13}\) onward. The Summary series is a solid blue line without markers, starting near 1.9 at \(2^9\), increasing sharply to about 4.7 at \(2^{11}\), dipping slightly around \(2^{12}\) (~4.5), then rising to about 5.7 at \(2^{15}\) and approaching about 6.0 by \(2^{18}\)–\(2^{20}\). The Law series is a solid yellow line without markers, beginning around 3.6 at \(2^9\), increasing to about 5.1 at \(2^{11}\), dropping near \(2^{12}\) (~4.6), then climbing to roughly 5.7–5.8 around \(2^{14}\) and reaching about 6.0 by \(2^{18}\)–\(2^{20}\). The Translation series is a solid purple line without markers, starting around 5.1 at \(2^9\), peaking early near \(2^{10}\) (~5.3), dipping around \(2^{11}\) (~4.7), then rising to about 5.6 at \(2^{12}\) and gradually increasing to about 6.0 by \(2^{18}\)–\(2^{20}\). The Code series is a solid gray line without markers, starting near 1.9 at \(2^9\), increasing to about 2.9 at \(2^{11}\) and ~3.7 at \(2^{13}\), dropping around \(2^{14}\) (~3.1), then rising steadily to about 4.8 at \(2^{16}\), ~5.3–5.4 at \(2^{17}\)–\(2^{18}\), and ending near 5.8 at \(2^{20}\). The Math series is a solid green line without markers, beginning around 3.8 at \(2^9\), increasing to about 4.7 at \(2^{11}\), then rising gradually through ~5.3 at \(2^{13}\), ~5.5 at \(2^{15}\), and approaching about 6.0 by \(2^{18}\)–\(2^{20}\).
